# Local convex bulges corrected by exponential inner erosion

This note proves a local, genuinely convex correction of a small bulge's
integer-base moment. It retains every positive fiber and pays less removed
mass than added mass when the added base mean is sufficiently interior.
It then gives the exact centroid-cap payment identity and an all-cap,
zero-slack example where the correction strictly improves the local depth
budget. It does not prove that an arbitrary maximum extraction admits
such a paid bulge, or any retained-mass fraction.

The removal-mass gauge agrees with the separate source-selection result
in `candidate d77abe6ff171c6f3`.
The new feature here is a small INNER PARALLEL correction of every fiber,
with a positive definite finite moment Jacobian, and the explicit active
cap payment in Sections 5--6. It is not a possibly macroscopic one-cap
replacement of the source.

## 1. Convexity of the correction

Let E be a compact convex set in R^n x R^d, d>=1, and let r(z)>=0 be a
convex function of the real base. Define

    E[-r]={(z,x): x+r(z) B_d subset E_z},             (1)

where B_d is the closed Euclidean unit ball. This is convex. Indeed, if
x_l+r(z_l)B_d subset E_zl for l=0,1, then convexity of E gives inclusion
of the Minkowski combination with radius (1-t)r(z_0)+t r(z_1). Convexity
of r makes that radius at least r((1-t)z_0+t z_1), proving (1).

In particular

    r(z)=s exp(v dot(z-j)),  s>0                    (2)

is allowed. At a fixed integer z this is ordinary inner parallel erosion.
If E is polyhedral, each corrected INTEGER fiber is still a polytope,
with the same candidate facet normals. Equivalently an ambient inequality

    a_f dot z+u_f dot x<=b_f

becomes

    a_f dot z+u_f dot x+s |u_f| exp(v dot(z-j))<=b_f.

Vertical inequalities, with u_f=0, stay unchanged. The corrected ambient
set need not be a polytope between integer bases; taking the convex hull
of its integer fibers restores a polyhedral representative when those
fibers are polytopes, with exactly the same mixed measure.

## 2. Exact small-loss moment range

Let D have finitely many positive full-dimensional fibers A_z, indexed
by a lattice-convex finite P, with true centroid (j,c), j integer. Work
in the k-dimensional affine span of P; put d_z=z-j in linear coordinates
on that span. The base point j is in ri(conv P). Write

    m=sum_z |A_z|,  S_z=H_(d-1)(boundary A_z)>0.

For d=1, S_z=2. Consider convex compatible enlargements E_t with exactly
these positive integer bases, A_z subset (E_t)_z, and

    (E_t)_z -> A_z in Hausdorff distance,
    delta_t=sum_z (|(E_t)_z|-|A_z|)>0,
    delta_t ->0.

Let r_t be the base centroid of their ADDED source, and suppose r_t->r.
Choose a fixed 0<kappa<1 for which

    r_loss=j+(r-j)/kappa is in ri(conv P).           (3)

Then for all sufficiently small t there exist s_t>0 and v_t such that
the removed source from the exponential erosion E_t[-r_tilde] has
EXACTLY

    removed mass=kappa delta_t,
    removed base moment about j=delta_t(r_t-j),      (4)

where r_tilde(z)=s_t exp(v_t dot d_z). Consequently its retained source
has true integer base centroid j and mass

    m+(1-kappa)delta_t>m.                           (5)

All positive fibers remain positive. The corrected body is contained in
E_t and hence in the original C whenever E_t subset C. If the base span
is proper, the already proved exact one-sided thickening realizes its
canonical positive-fiber hull by an ambient body without changing any
integer trace.

Here is a proof which includes local existence, rather than only formal
moment equations. For parameters h in R and v in R^k put

    radius_z=delta exp(h+v dot d_z),
    R_(t,z)(h,v)=
       [|(E_t)_z|-|(E_t)_z inner-eroded by radius_z|]/delta,
    q_z=(1,d_z),
    F_t(h,v)=sum_z q_z R_(t,z)(h,v),                 (6)

with delta=delta_t. On every compact parameter set, these maps converge
in C^1 to

    F_0(h,v)=sum_z S_z exp(h+v dot d_z) q_z.         (7)

For clarity, the elementary parallel-body facts used here are

    |K|-|K inner-eroded by a|=
       integral_0^a H_(d-1)(boundary(K inner-eroded by b)) db,

and continuity of convex surface area under Hausdorff convergence while
an inball stays positive. The first identity is the coarea formula for
distance to the boundary. The second follows, for example, from the
Cauchy projection formula; in the polyhedral setting it also follows by
summing the areas of converging or splitting facets. All finitely many
fibers have a common positive lower inradius for small t. Their eroded
sets converge uniformly to A_z for radii tending to zero. Differentiating
(6) with respect to h and v therefore gives precisely the C^1 convergence
claimed in (7). No differentiability in the bulge parameter t is needed.

There is a unique (h_0,v_0) solving

    F_0(h_0,v_0)=(kappa,r-j).                       (8)

Indeed minimizing

    log(sum_z S_z exp(v dot d_z))
      -v dot((r-j)/kappa)

is coercive and strictly convex on R^k: the prescribed mean is in the
relative interior and P spans that space. This gives v_0; choose h_0 to
make the total weight kappa. The Jacobian at (h_0,v_0) is

    J=sum_z S_z exp(h_0+v_0 dot d_z) q_z q_z^T,       (9)

which is positive definite because the q_z span R^(k+1).

Uniform C^1 convergence now proves the exact equations. More explicitly,
on a small fixed parameter ball the map

    x -> x-J^(-1)[F_t(x)-(kappa,r_t-j)]

is a contraction and maps the ball to itself for sufficiently small t.
Its fixed point supplies (4). This proves the asserted exact correction.
The proof is uniform if the desired loss means stay in a compact subset
of ri(conv P).

The construction has no dependence on beta. Its parameters can blow up
when r_loss approaches the boundary; no uniform boundary statement is
claimed. The geometric condition (3) is explicit: any kappa strictly
larger than the Minkowski gauge of r-j in conv(P)-j suffices. If r is on
an exposed boundary face, a single added source concentrated there cannot
in general be balanced by removing LESS mass from P; applying that face's
exposing affine functional proves the obstruction immediately.

## 3. An actual unused point gives a small correctable bulge at an interior base

Here assume the canonical D is polyhedral. Suppose z_0 belongs to
ri(conv P) intersect Z^n and C_z0 strictly contains A_z0. Choose a segment
inside C_z0 from an interior point of A_z0 to an unused point. A generic
choice meets a relative facet interior of A_z0 at x_0. Let

    p_t=(z_0,x_0+t w),  E_t=conv(D union {p_t}),

for small t>0, with w pointing into the unused part of C_z0. Then E_t
subset C, its base projection is conv P, and its added mixed mass tends
to zero. Its own z_0-fiber contains a pyramid with fixed positive
(d-1)-dimensional base and height proportional to t, so its added volume
is at least c_0 t for some c_0>0 (for d=1 this is simply an interval
extension).

The total added mixed volume is at most C_0 t. One direct proof uses a
finite inequality representation of D: every old facet inequality is
violated by p_t by at most O(t), so E_t is contained in the polytope
obtained by relaxing all those inequalities by O(t). At each of the
finitely many integer bases the fiber is full-dimensional. A fixed
interior point converts this relaxed fiber into a homothetic O(t)
expansion of A_z, giving an O(t) volume increase. Summing proves the claim.

Thus a fixed positive fraction of the added mass lies at z_0. The added
base means stay in a compact subset of ri(conv P): if
B(z_0,epsilon) in conv P in its relative affine span and the fraction is
at least theta>0, then B(r_t,theta epsilon) in conv P. A single kappa<1
sufficiently near one makes (3) hold uniformly. Section 2 therefore
corrects this ACTUAL bulge with a strict net mass gain.

This is only a BASE-centroid correction. The local depth constraint
still has to be paid. The next two sections give the precise cost.

## 4. Exact cap payment and a uniform sufficient bound

Write nu_t for the added source E_t minus D and rho_t for the removed
source from E_t. Their masses are delta and kappa delta, respectively,
and (4) gives

    integral (z-j) d(nu_t-rho_t)=0.

The corrected source has mass m'=m+(1-kappa)delta and continuous centroid
c'. Its exact displacement is

    c'-c= [integral (x-c) d(nu_t-rho_t)]/m'.         (10)

Fix a nonvertical through-old-centroid margin

    L(z,x)=a dot(z-j)+u dot(x-c),  |u|=1,
    H_t={L>=t},   t_H=u dot(c'-c).

Then H_(t_H) passes through the NEW centroid and, by base balance,

    t_H=[integral L d(nu_t-rho_t)]/m'.              (11)

For ANY beta the exact deficit identity is

    mu_new(H_(t_H))-beta m'
      = [mu_D(H_0)-beta m]
        +nu_t(H_(t_H))-rho_t(H_(t_H))
        -beta(1-kappa)delta
        +mu_D(H_(t_H))-mu_D(H_0).                  (12)

No cap-boundary mass has been discarded. Vertical caps use t_H=0 and
the same source-addition/removal formula.

For a completely uniform, although sometimes coarse, sufficient test,
let sigma be the old absolute depth slack above beta m. Let

    R=max{|x-c|: z in P,x in C_z},
    L_0=sum_z sup_(|u|=1,b) H_(d-1)(A_z intersect {u dot x=b}).

Both are finite; in d=1 take L_0=|P|. A fiber contained in a radius-R_z
ball contributes at most vol_(d-1)(B_(d-1)) R_z^(d-1) to L_0.
Equation (10) gives |c'-c|<=R(1+kappa)delta/m'. Coarea bounds the loss of
old cap mass by L_0|c'-c|, while the removed source costs at most kappa
delta. Thus the corrected body remains locally beta-deep whenever

    [beta(1-kappa)+kappa]delta
      +L_0 R(1+kappa)delta/[m+(1-kappa)delta]
      <=sigma.                                    (13)

All constants stay finite as beta increases to gamma_d, provided the
geometric data and kappa stay fixed. Formula (13) proves that a maximum
extraction with STRICT depth slack cannot have the unused interior-base
bulge of Section 3. It does not by itself treat zero slack.

## 5. The active-cap influence function, with exact moments retained

For a sharper first-order test, suppose along a subsequence

    nu_t/delta -> nu,    rho_t/delta -> rho

weakly. Here nu has mass one, rho has mass kappa, and their signed base
moment about j is zero. In the polyhedral setting the erosion law is
explicit:

    rho=sum_z exp(h_0+v_0 dot d_z)
                  H_(d-1) restricted to boundary A_z.             (14)

This follows from the inner-layer formula used in Section 2, including
the position variable; facets contribute their normal boundary layers
and lower-dimensional edges contribute o(delta).

For a fixed margin L assume its plane contains no positive-area fiber
facet, and nu and rho give the plane mass zero. The original cap profile
is then differentiable at zero, with derivative -S_H, where

    S_H=sum_z H_(d-1)(A_z intersect {L=0}).

At an ACTIVE old cap, mu_D(H_0)=beta m, differentiating the exact identity
(12) gives

    lim [mu_new(H_(t_H))-beta m']/delta
       = integral W_H d(nu-rho),
    W_H=1_(L>=0)-beta-(S_H/m)L.                    (15)

The integer coefficient a is legitimately included in L because the
signed source correction has zero BASE moment. Also

    integral W_H dmu_D=0.                          (16)

The last equality uses both active mass and the TRUE full centroid.
This is a sign-bearing payment function, not just a multiplier list.
For S_H>0 it is nonnegative on the included band
0<=L<=(1-beta)m/S_H, and also on the sufficiently far EXCLUDED side
L<=-beta m/S_H. Added mass outside a cap can therefore pay its deficit
through the centroid shift; merely discarding that contribution loses
information.

At coincident facets use the exact identity (12) or its one-sided strip
limits; formula (15) is not asserted with an arbitrary trace convention.
Nor does pointwise positivity for a few selected caps establish the
all-cap condition. Section 6 supplies a complete example where every
cap is checked directly.

## 6. Exact zero-slack example with payment of ALL active caps

Take n=d=1 and bases z=-1,0,1,2. Let D have centered interval fibers
with lengths

    (5,9/2,3,1).

Its upper endpoints (5/2,9/4,3/2,1/2) form a concave sequence; its lower
endpoints are their negatives and form a convex sequence. Use their
piecewise affine interpolation, or the convex hull of the integer
fibers, as the actual ambient body. Its mass is 27/2 and its true
centroid is (0,0), since -5+3+2=0.

For 0<=delta<=1/4, enlarge ONLY the upper endpoint of the z=1 fiber by
delta. These remain compatible fibers: their upper slopes are
-1/4, -3/4+delta, -1-delta. Denote this convex enlargement by E_delta,
and take the original available body C=E_(1/4).

Now erode the fiber at z by the radius

    radius_z=delta 2^z/19.                          (17)

The real-base radius is convex, so Section 1 proves compatibility and
containment in C. The exact removed masses at the four bases are

    delta(1,2,4,8)/19.

Their mass is 15delta/19, and their first base moment is
(-1+4+16)delta/19=delta, exactly the moment of the addition at base1.
Thus kappa=15/19, the net mass gain is 4delta/19, and the new base
centroid stays exactly zero. The corrected endpoints are

    l=(-5/2+delta/38, -9/4+delta/19,
       -3/2+2delta/19, -1/2+4delta/19),
    r=( 5/2-delta/38,  9/4-delta/19,
        3/2+17delta/19, 1/2-4delta/19).             (18)

They have exact total mass and continuous centroid

    m_delta=27/2+4delta/19,
    c_delta=3delta(5delta+19)/(8delta+513).           (19)

Here is an all-real-slope depth proof. An upward through-centroid cap
x+a z>=c_delta has mass

    F_delta(a)=sum_z clamp(r_z+a z-c_delta,0,r_z-l_z).

The six nonconstant clipping breakpoints, in increasing order, are

    l_-1-c, c-r_1, (c-r_2)/2,
    (c-l_2)/2, c-l_1, r_-1-c.                       (20)

Their consecutive differences are strictly positive on [0,1/4]. After
putting over positive denominators their numerators are, respectively,

    860delta^2-13319delta+19494,
    2delta^2+1978delta+2565,
    19-8delta,
    30delta^2+154delta+2565,
    19494-2489delta-1116delta^2.

The first and last are positive even after replacing each negative term
by its worst value at delta=1/4; the other three are immediate. Between
these breakpoints F_delta has successive slopes

    0, -1, 0, 2, 0, -1, 0.

The z=0 contribution is proper throughout. It follows that the absolute
nonvertical depth is the minimum of exactly four expressions:

    Q_1=w_1+w_2+r_0-c,
    Q_2=m_delta-(r_-1+r_0+r_1+w_2-3c),
    Q_3=m_delta-(w_-1+r_0-c),
    Q_4=r_-1+r_0+r_1-3c,                            (21)

where w_z=r_z-l_z. Opposite nonvertical caps have complementary mass,
so these four minima include both orientations and every real slope.
Vertical closed caps contain the WHOLE z=0 fiber and dominate the
corresponding finite-tilt limits. They cannot lower (21).

At delta=0 all four quantities equal 25/4. Therefore the original true
centroid has EXACT depth

    beta=(25/4)/(27/2)=25/54<gamma_1=1/2.            (22)

For the corrected source, the four exact deficits Q_i-beta m_delta are

    delta(28215-6799delta)/[513(8delta+513)],
    delta(43858delta+27189)/[1026(8delta+513)],
    delta(8591delta+86697)/[513(8delta+513)],
    delta(202635-40274delta)/[1026(8delta+513)].      (23)

Every expression is STRICTLY POSITIVE for 0<delta<=1/4. Thus the convex
correction gains mass while making the true integer centroid strictly
MORE than beta-deep against EVERY closed ambient halfspace. This is a
zero-slack example, not an invocation of the sufficient slack bound.

The first-order deficits in (23) are

    55/513, 53/1026, 169/513, 395/1026.

In particular every active cap family is paid, with minimum derivative
53/1026. In the influence formula (15), the added law is the point mass
at (1,3/2), and the removal law puts equal weights at the two endpoints
of each original interval, with base totals (1,2,4,8)/19. These reproduce
all four derivatives, including the beneficial signed centroid term.
At the clipping endpoints themselves the direct formulas (20)--(23)
handle the coincident traces and prevent a hidden exceptional slope.

This example shows that the constructive correction can pay an active
local-depth constraint. It is not a counterexample to extraction
maximality: D is explicitly improved inside C. For a general maximum
extraction the sign of (12) or (15) for all active caps is still the
substantive unsolved condition. Neither normalization of contact stress
nor the mass/base correction alone implies that sign.

## 7. The paid examples persist up to beta increasing to gamma_1

The previous calibration extends to a>=3 by using centered original
fiber lengths

    (a+2, 3a/2, a, 1)

at the same four bases. Its mass and exact true-centroid depth are

    M_a=(7a+6)/2,
    beta_a=(7a+4)/[2(7a+6)] increasing to 1/2.       (24)

Again raise only the z=1 upper endpoint by delta and use the SAME
radii delta 2^z/19, for 0<delta<=1/4. Compatibility follows from the
successive upper slopes a/4-1, -a/4+delta, 1/2-a/2-delta. Their order
holds for a>=3 on this whole delta interval. The exact corrected mass
and centroid are

    m=M_a+4delta/19,
    c=delta(19a+15delta)/(133a+8delta+114).           (25)

The same six-event order and four-cap classification (20)--(21) hold.
Put P=133a+8delta+114. The four deficits, divided by delta, have
positive denominators 19(7a+6)P, 38(7a+6)P, 19(7a+6)P,
38(7a+6)P, respectively, and numerators

    1197a^2+4750a+3192-delta(1771a+1486),
    4921a^2-3496a-6612+delta(11354a+9796),
    6251a^2+9082a+3192+delta(2219a+1934),
    9975a^2+31160a+19380-delta(10458a+8900).          (26)

These are strictly positive for a>=3, 0<=delta<=1/4. For the second,
the delta-free quadratic is positive and increasing from a=3; all
others remain positive after replacing negative delta terms by their
values at delta=1/4. The event-order numerators, over positive
denominators, are

    5054a+4332-delta(3211a+3686)+860delta^2,
    266a^2+95a-114+510a delta+2delta^2+448delta,
    19-8delta,
    266a^2+95a-114+(54a-8)delta+30delta^2,
    5054a+4332-1045a delta+646delta-1116delta^2.

The same elementary bounds prove all five positive. Thus (26) is an
all-cap strict payment for the entire parameter range, not just a
fixed-normal derivative statement.

The first-order deficits are

    (9a+28)/[19(7a+6)],
    (37a-58)/[38(7a+6)],
    (47a+28)/[19(7a+6)],
    5(15a+34)/[38(7a+6)].                           (27)

All are at least 53/1026 for a>=3: the first decreases to 9/133,
the second increases from 53/1026, and the third and fourth dominate
the first and second respectively. Therefore the absolute first-order
cap-payment constants do not collapse as beta_a increases to gamma_1.
The original and available bodies change with a; this does NOT supply
a limiting improvement at a fixed gamma_1-maximal body.

In fact an unconditional improvement at such a body is false. See
`candidate 97b12ef4ecc6c56e`:
an exactly maximal half-depth extraction of mass12 has unused source
in its own interior integer fiber, and its simplest upper bulge has
negative active-cap deficit -t(3+t)/(12+t). The exact maximum is above
the desired retained threshold. The additional below-threshold
hypothesis, if useful, still has to enter an unproved global argument.
